analytic.title: Performance Evaluation of the Weakly Hard Real-Time Tasks for Global Multiprocessor Scheduling Approach

div.p: Real-time systems can be classified into three categories, based on the "seriousness" of deadline misses either by hard, soft, or weakly hard real-time tasks. The consequences of deadlines miss for a hard real-time task cannot be tolerated because some failure can affect the system performance whereas some deadline misses can be tolerated for soft real-time tasks. Meanwhile, in a weakly hard real-time task, the distribution of its met and missed deadlines is stated and specified precisely. Due to the complexity and significantly increased functionality in system computation, attention has been given to multiprocessor scheduling. Studies have shown that current multiprocessor scheduling of weakly hard real-time tasks used imprecise computation model based on iterative algorithms. This algorithm decomposed into two parts; mandatory and optional parts, unfortunately, the result analysis is precise only if its mandatory and optional parts are both executed. Even, the use of hierarchical scheduling algorithm, such as two-level scheduling under PFair algorithm may cause high overhead due to frequent preemptions and migrations. Furthermore, this algorithm incurs significant run-time overhead due to their quantum-based scheduling. In order to cater for the limitations and stated problems, an alternative multiprocessor scheduling approach, called global scheduling is proposed. The proposed scheduling approach aims to improve the probability of deadline satisfactions as much as possible and at the same time achieve a higher utilization of the task sets, with less task migrations. Thus, in this paper, performance measurement parameters are used as performance evaluation of the proposed scheduling approach.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: A real-time system has two notions of correctness: logical and temporal. Particularly, in addition to producing correct outputs (logical correctness), such a system needs to ensure that these outputs are produced at the correct time (temporal correctness).

Real-time systems can be classified into three categories, based on the "seriousness" of deadline misses either by hard, soft or weakly hard real-time tasks. In this paper, weakly hard real-time tasks have been studied rather than hard and soft realtime tasks because "weakly hard" precisely define and specify the distribution of missed and met deadlines for the tasks during a given time period.

In the past, much of research efforts have been focused on scheduling and schedulability analysis or tests of uniprocessor system, as well as in weakly hard real-time scheduling. This is mainly due to the fact that scheduling algorithms for multiprocessor are significantly more complex than for uniprocessor. Since, the scheduling algorithm must not only specify an execution ordering of tasks, but must also determine the specific processor to be used. Scheduling is the allocation time to tasks, and a scheduling algorithm is used for determining such allocation. Meanwhile, a schedulability analysis or tests for a given scheduling algorithm accepts as input the specifications of a real-time systems, and determines whether the scheduling algorithm can guarantee to schedule the system such that all tasks will meet all deadlines or not.

Conventional multiprocessor scheduling can be classified as either partitioned or global scheduling of tasks [1]. In partitioning scheduling, each task is allocated to a specific processor permanently or in other words, an execution of the task is permitted only on that processor with no migration and each processor independently schedules its assigned tasks using a uniprocessor scheduling algorithm. And, in the partitioning multiprocessor scheduling, usually, divided a task set into groups beforehand. Then, a separate ready queue holds by each processor such that a specific processor is assigned by each task group. In global scheduling, task preemptions and migrations are permitted, that is a task preempted on a particular processor may resume execution on the same or on a different processor. Additionally, in global multiprocessor scheduling, need to allocate the available processors to the highest priority task in the ready queue.

A typical example of systems with weakly hard real-time requirements is multimedia systems, such as videophone application because some delay during execution is acceptable in that system and it is unnecessary to meet all the tasks deadlines as long as the misses (or deadlines) are specified precisely. In a weakly hard real-time system, the number of deadlines that may be missed can be specified. Such weakly hard real-time scheduling approach has traditionally focused upon scheduling analysis on uniprocessor. As a system becomes more complex and significantly increasing functionality, attention has been given to multiprocessor scheduling, comprised of several processors. Research on multiprocessor scheduling has mainly focused on ensuring strict compliance deadlines and several scheduling techniques were adopted. In an effort, Carpenter et al. have cataloged multiprocessor real-time scheduling algorithm considers the degree of migration jobs or tasks and the complexity of the mechanism of priority [1]. The classes of priorities includes such as (a) static priority, where task priorities are never change, Rate Monotonic Algorithm (RMA); (b) dynamic priority, where job or task priorities are change dynamically, Earliest Deadline First (EDF).

div.head: II. RELATED WORK
div.p: There have been some efforts to schedule weakly hard realtime tasks on multiprocessor systems. Wu and Jin proposed the classical weakly hard real-time scheduling algorithms, namely Distance Based Priority (DBP), which originally was introduced by [2] on uniprocessor system, to apply into multiprocessor applications to guarantee QoS of both hard real-time tasks and multimedia streams even under overload conditions [3]. However, MPDBPs cannot maximize the performance and satisfaction ratio of the task deadline when the system is under loaded or even when possible, and consequently, the quality of service for applications of multimedia streaming is ultimately fails to be good as provided.

Another work is done by Kong and Cho [4] wherein they proposed the first dynamic real-time scheduling algorithm for (m,k)-firm deadline constrained tasks on homogenous multiprocessors to guarantee the performance of algorithm, called the Guaranteed Multiprocessor Real-Time Scheduling (GMRTS-MK) algorithm. However, the algorithm that they use will cause an increase in the ratio caused by the increasing number of tasks. Later, the same author, Kong and Cho [5] introduced an Energy-constrained Multiprocessor Real-Time Scheduling (EMRTS-MK) class algorithms for weakly hard real-time for (m,k)-firm deadline constrained tasks running on multiprocessor.

Several static and dynamic approaches on global multiprocessor scheduling have been proposed but most prior research is limits for hard and soft real-time tasks. The most well-known static priority scheduling algorithm is hybrid priority assignment like Rate Monotonic with Utilization Separation (RM-US) [6], that obtain much better scheduling performances and scheduling the remaining ones with RMA. Thereafter, Pathan and Jonsson [7] proposed a priority assignment for global fixed priority scheduling, called the Fixed-Priority Test (FPT) test. Later, Back et al, [8] presented a new schedulability analysis approach, called the Earliest-Quasi-Deadline-First (EQDF) algorithm. EQDF assigns priority to jobs according to their quasi-deadlines.

Bertogna and Cirinei [9] adapted response time analysis by iteratively computing an upper bound on the response time of each task. Further, Guan et al, [10] extended the response time analysis of [9]. Sun et al. [11] address the problem of schedulability analysis for a set of sporadic tasks with arbitrary deadlines running on a multiprocessor system with global fixedpriority preemptive scheduling.

Proportionate-fair (Pfair) [12], which uses a quantum based model is known as an optimal scheduling algorithm for global scheduling. However, this algorithm will generate a number of task preemptions and migration overhead and it is very complex to implement. There are some simple dynamic priority scheduling algorithm which perform fairly well with a small number of task preemptions and migration overhead, such as Earliest Deadline First with Utilization Separation (EDF-US). But, much better in order to achieve performances of scheduling for multiprocessor systems is Earliest Deadline until Zero Laxity (EDZL) [13]. Nevertheless, their utilization bounds for schedulable systems are just 50%.

Based on the review, research efforts on scheduling weakly hard real-time tasks on multiprocessor are relatively promising area of research. Previous works have investigated how to predict the temporal behavior and to determine whether the timing requirements of an application tasks will be met. However, many of their works are extremely applied on hard real-time tasks. Studies have shown that some researchers has adopted the approach of using response time analysis in global scheduling. But, it is limited to sporadic task sets. Hence, this paper finds a solution to schedule periodic weakly hard real-time tasks by applying multiprocessor response time analysis. designations.

div.head: III. THE GLOBAL SCHEDULING AND HYPERPERIOD ANALYSIS
div.p: In the global approach [1], migration is allowed; where during execution, migration of the tasks among processors is permitted arbitrarily. There have two level of migration for global scheduling. Job level migration means each job of a task can be run on any processor. But a job started on a given processor cannot be moved on another. Task level migration where a task can run at any time on any processor. The advantages of using global scheduling algorithms, tasks are dynamically assigned to the available processing units, and it can succeed in meeting deadlines. Response time analysis (RTA) is an effective technique that has been widely used to derive schedulability tests and properties for various different models of task systems scheduled on uniprocessor. Another alternative to study the performance of a scheduling algorithm, or to verify the schedulability of a task set, is through the use of an exact analysis such as hyperperiod analysis. Similarly, it can be used to verify if a task set misses any deadline, showing if it is unschedulable. Also, it can be used as a sufficient condition for unschedulability.

The task set hyperperiod (0, H(τ )) is a feasibility interval for implicit and constrained deadline synchronous periodic tasksets, when scheduled by a deterministic and memoryless algorithm, such as Rate Monotonic Algorithm (RMA) [16]. For these algorithms, the schedulability of the task set can be verified by checking if the schedule generated misses any deadline using the least common multiple calculation. It is possible to use hyperperiod analysis on multiprocessor scheduling because of using periodic task with deadline and preemptive fixed priority scheduling.

div.head: IV. A SCHEDULABILITY ANALYSIS IN GLOBAL SCHEDULING
div.p: Real-time scheduling analysis involves a mathematical verification of whether there are potential timing problems or not in the system. The equation appears very complex, but they are usually quite simple to implement when all the data is available. The system behaves in global scheduling as explained in detail as follows. The processor is assigned with each task in order to assign a local (for a processor) with static priority. An upper bound of the response time of a task τi in a multiprocessor system scheduled with fixed priority can be derived by the fixedpoint iteration on the value Ri, starting with Ri = Ci. We determine whether a set of tasks allocated to a processor is schedulable given a particular fixed priority assignment by checking whether the worst-case response time for each task is less than or equal to its relative deadline. Although there has one task missed its deadline in the worst case, however, it is weakly hard schedulable.

V. PERFORMANCE EVALUATION This section evaluates the performance guarantee expressed in terms of deadline satisfaction ratio of the proposed approach. The performance of the proposed approach consists of analysing and comparing with the existing approach, namely MPDBPs, GMRTS-MK and EMRTS-MK. This is carried out by using randomly generated task sets with system utilization varying from 0 to 2 and the number of tasks ranges from 2 to 10 through simulation. The primary metric for evaluation is deadline satisfaction ratio or success ratio.

The global scheduler runs in one of the processors for assigning the tasks in the processors using a given algorithm. Then, in each processor the proposed and existing approaches are executed. In this case, the overall system utilization is varied from 0 to 2 with an increment of 0.05. The graphical representation of deadline satisfaction ratio between the proposed and existing competitive approaches is shown in Fig. 3(a) and 3(b). From both figures, we can observe that the proposed scheduling approach outperforms the others. In Fig. 3(a), when system utilization is 1.5, the proposed scheduling approach can achieve a success ratio around 0.99. This is an improvement of 29% over MPDBPs (0.8) and GMRTS-MK (0.9), and improvement of 2.5 times over EMRTS-MK (0.65). Thus, in the proposed scheduling approach, the number of deadlines misses for the tasks are reduced.

When the processor utilization is increased and increasing the number of tasks in the test set, the deadline misses ratio increases. This performance analysis is graphically shown in Fig. 3(b). The average miss ratio is higher in EMRTS-MK compared to GMRTS-MK and MPDBPs. This is much reduced in the proposed approach (almost 20%) compared to the existing approaches. The main reason for this is that when using a schedulability test based on response time analysis for the global approach, the increasing of success ratio can be expected. Thus, the proposed approach results in a lower deadline miss ratio compared to the existing ones. This is due to the count task miss for the proposed approach being less than the others. In fact, the simulation shows that at every percentage of utilization, the proposed approach also achieves a higher satisfaction ratio when the number of tasks is increased. The multiprocessor response time is calculated and checked to ensure that the deadline was met. If the task does not meet its deadline, then checking of weakly hard constraint and µ-pattern must be carried out. Both analyses lead to the proposed approach obtaining better results than the existing approaches.

In conclusion, the performance of the proposed approach was evaluated in terms of the deadline satisfaction ratio based on the system utilization and the number of tasks. For comparison, MDPBPs, GMRTS-MK and EMRTS-MK were considered as existing approaches on multiprocessor scheduling. Experimental results show that the proposed scheduling approach led to decreases the deadline misses or in other words, achieved higher success ratio. Based on experimental results, it can be concluded that the approach can be useful on any multiprocessor system whose worst-case bound delays can be obtained.

div.head: VI. CONCLUSION
div.p: As conclusion, this study has described the schedulability analysis of weakly hard real-time tasks on multiprocessor. The results analyses were investigated through an experiment with the AMR case study. In this paper, we presented an offline static schedulability analysis in order to schedule periodic weakly hard real-time tasks. We have been focused on global scheduling approach.

From the comparison results, the proposed global approach has a higher satisfaction ratio in term of system utilization and number of tasks. This is due to assigned tasks based on priority order under the Rate-Monotonic. Based on the utilization of a task set on two (2) processors, show that the proposed global approach outperforms the others due to maximizing the schedulability of soft tasks. This is because of the usage of hyperperiod analysis and deadline models. This is due to a task can meeting its deadline at different invocations in the hyperperiod (least common multiple of the tasks periods) even though it does not do so in the worst case.

The proposed global approach use multiprocessor response time tests to check if allocation is possible for all unassigned tasks. The response time is one of the scheduling bounds which ensure that a task set is schedulable. The deadlines are allowed to be missed provided the extent of such misses is bounded (hence response times are bounded as well). Motivated by these results, it is possible to specify reasonable constraints under which bounded response times can be guaranteed using global real-time scheduling techniques, for periodic task systems that are weakly hard in nature.

The test results show that, although systems with global schedulability analysis techniques would be unschedulable in the worst case, they can be weakly hard schedulable. This can be attributed to three ways which lead to that result. The first one involves computing the upper bounds for the response times of each invocation of the tasks. The second one calculates the least common multiple for the tasksets. The third one checks that the resulting such μ-pattern satisfies the constraints. Most importantly, from the performance evaluation results, it proved that the proposed approach satisfied the task deadlines and timing constraints with a smaller number of misses. The reason can be attributed to the distribution of lost deadlines being predictable in using weakly hard models.

Regarding this approach, designers can provide more predictable weakly hard real-time systems based on using weakly hard scheduling technique consists of exact analysis such as hyperperiod analysis combining with deadline models or temporal constraints, namely weakly hard constraints, and µpatterns. Also, our approach can be useful on any multiprocessor system whose worst-case bound delays can be obtained. This is due to for weakly hard constraints, if any given constraint is remains unsatisfied, there is possibility to calculate and create a set of constraints that may be satisfied instead. Thus, by using deadline models, it avoiding serious consequences result due to systems are not complete in a timely.
